assumptions: The root adds 'input logic shared_write_prefetch_i' and 'output logic dbg_shared_write_prefetch_ready' to the ACTUAL_DMA_SYSTEM top (nonblock_actual_dma_system_top.sv).  The two driver assignments are therefore placed inside '#ifdef ACTUAL_DMA_SYSTEM', mirroring the §57 shared_source_cutover_i precedent.  If the root also adds the input to the non-SYSTEM top (Vnonblock_actual_dma_top), the parent may move those two lines out of the #ifdef (harness §51 pattern used for shared_read_quantum_i / shared_write_keep_q_i); the CLI parse and the validation stay system-only either way.

dbg_shared_write_prefetch_ready is a sticky 1-bit observation: 1 once the real A second-destination-page WRITE recipe was successfully prepared, held until reset, independent of the later job end / cache-valid deassertion.  If the RTL only pulses this output, the new terminal CHECK (5c) can fail spuriously - flagged for Codex/root.
The harness makes NO assertion when +write-prefetch=0, and NO assertion when +write-prefetch=1 but +a-dst-offset=0 (the task only asks to expect the seen flag when opt-in AND A offset nonzero).

+a-dst-offset is restricted to 8-byte multiples because the copy is AXI-beat (8 B) aligned; 2056 = 0x808 is the smallest aligned value that really crosses the first destination page (F = 255), 4088 = 0xFF8 is the largest (F = 1).  Every accepted nonzero value yields the same derived next-page leaf PTE address 0x70048 (A L0 index 9).
'mode2' in the design document == task_physical_bypass == 2 in this harness.

No memory model, page-table image, payload constant, PTE-delay mechanism or pre-existing CHECK is changed; the only widened behaviour is the +a-dst-offset acceptance set plus the two rewritten error strings/comments.

nat_report_write_prefetch_json() is called unconditionally from nat_verify_and_report(); its body is compiled only for ACTUAL_DMA_SYSTEM and the #else branch keeps the (void)beats; idiom, so both build variants stay warning-free.
suggested_checks: Uniqueness: for each replacement, verify the old string occurs exactly once, e.g. perl -0777 -ne 'print scalar(() = /\Q...\E/g)' -F style grep -c; pay specific attention to the §57 static decl lines (they carry FOUR leading spaces in the file: '    static bool cutover_require_opt = false;   // +cutover-require=0|1').
Build both variants (-DACTUAL_DMA_SYSTEM and plain) to confirm the new printf compiles in both and that no missing port breaks the non-system build.

Regression (old offsets unchanged): +natural=1 +shared-source=1 +natural-bytes=2048 +a-dst-offset=3072 (+a-next-pte-delay=N) and +a-dst-offset=4088 must still pass exactly as before, with a_next_pte_delay_applied == 1 and a_next_pte_addr == 0x70048, and NATURAL-JSON first_a_page_beats = 128 / 1, a_first_raw_parent_bytes_expected = 1024 / 8.

New offsets: run +a-dst-offset = 2056, 2560, 3072, 4080, 4088.  Expect NATURAL-JSON a_cross_page=1, a_effective_dst_offset equal to the request, first_a_page_beats = 255, 192, 128, 2, 1 and a_first_raw_parent_bytes_expected = 2040, 1536, 1024, 16, 8; all byte checks (copied payload, untouched head/tail, V/A source unchanged), nat_pr/nat_pw geometry, hw issue/done == 1 and the derived next-PTE address 0x70048 must hold.

Rejection matrix for +a-dst-offset: 2048 (aligned, does not cross), 2050 (not 8-aligned), 2052, 4096, 4097, 99999 -> exit code 2 with the new message 'must be 0 or an 8-byte aligned offset in 2056..4088'.  Also +a-dst-offset=2056 without +natural=1/+shared-source=1 -> exit 2 (existing guard).

PTE delay: +a-next-pte-delay=500 with +a-dst-offset=2056 and with +a-dst-offset=4080 -> must pass with a_next_pte_delay_applied==1; +a-next-pte-delay=500 with +a-dst-offset=0 -> exit 2 with the new message.

+write-prefetch rejection matrix (each alone must exit 2 with its own message): missing +natural=1; missing +shared-source=1; +natural-bytes=32768; +physical-bypass=0/1/3; +shared-write-keep-q=0; +source-cutover=1; +pause-mode=1; and +write-prefetch=2 / +write-prefetch=x.

Happy path: +natural=1 +shared-source=1 +natural-bytes=2048 +physical-bypass=2 +shared-write-keep-q=1 +a-dst-offset=2056 (+a-next-pte-delay=<N> optional) +write-prefetch=1 -> must pass and print WRITE-PREFETCH-JSON with opt_in=1 and actual_future_write_success_seen=1, placed AFTER NATURAL-JSON, PLACEMENT-METRICS-JSON, SHARE50-JSON, SHARE51-REPEAT-JSON, MEMORY-R-INTERLEAVE-TERMINAL-JSON and SOURCE-SPONSOR-HANDOVER-JSON; a NEXT/WRITE peer must have the same a_next_pte_addr 0x70048.
Negative evidence path: same command with +write-prefetch=0 -> WRITE-PREFETCH-JSON opt_in=0 and no CHECK depends on the register (run must not fail merely because the register stays 0).

Confirm the terminal report is only emitted after all original checks: force a failure (e.g. wrong +a-dst-offset alignment or an injected byte mismatch) and verify no WRITE-PREFETCH-JSON success line is printed.
